Vaccine Protection and Waning by Vaccination Stratum

Source: R/vaccination_inputs.R
vaccine_strata_parameters.Rd

Assigns the protection and waning values of the vaccine parameter table to the model's vaccination strata.

Usage

vaccine_strata_parameters(vaccine_parameters, n_vacc, vaccine_waning = TRUE)

Arguments

vaccine_parameters

Vaccine parameter table for one disease, with columns `parameter`, `value`, `dose`.

n_vacc

Number of vaccination strata in the model.

vaccine_waning

Logical; if `FALSE` vaccine protection does not wane (both waning rates are zero and everyone stays in the short-term stratum of their last dose).

Value

A list with `protection`, `short_term_waning` and `long_term_waning` (vectors of length `n_vacc`; waning as daily probabilities) and `table`, a data frame describing each dose.

Details

The model has one unvaccinated stratum (1) and two strata per dose. Dose `d` is given into its short-term stratum (index `2d + 1`), which wanes at `short_term_waning` into its long-term stratum (index `2d`), which in turn wanes at `long_term_waning` to unvaccinated. So short-term protection belongs on the odd strata and long-term protection on the even strata.

In 0.1.0 the two were swapped, the row of the table was chosen by comparing the stratum index (not the dose) with the table's `dose`, so that both measles doses used the second-dose row and one pertussis stratum was given the sum of two rows (a protection of 1.75), and a single waning rate (the slowest in the table) was used for every stratum.

The table has two rows of doses per disease (measles 1 and 2; diphtheria 1 and 6; pertussis 3 and 5) while the model has two measles doses and three DTP doses. Each modelled dose uses its own row if there is one and the first row otherwise. For measles that is simply dose 1 and dose 2. For DTP the `dose` tag is the number of doses received when the estimate applies: the first row (diphtheria 1, pertussis 3) is the three-dose primary series and the second (diphtheria 6, pertussis 5) the full schedule including boosters, which the model does not represent. So all three DTP doses get the primary-series row. That overstates protection after one or two doses; values for partial courses belong in the table as their own rows (with `dose` 1 and 2), not in code.
